# 1 Epidemiological highlights

• Epidemiological situation: No new affected health zone has been reported.
The cumulative total remains at 47 affected health zones out of 140 in the five provinces, of which 46 remain in active transmission.

• Coordination: Arrival of the new National Incident Manager (IM) in Bunia, Professor Steve Ahuka; The Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare as well as Professor Pierre Akilimali (IM) were received in audience by the President of Uganda on 22 July 2026 to review the situation of the Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (MVE-B 17); Harmonisation of epidemiological data between the provinces of Ituri and Nord-Kivu and the national level.

• Evolution of cases: During the last 24 hours, 97 new confirmed cases, 62 confirmed deaths and 13 recoveries were recorded:

o Ituri: 73 new confirmed cases were reported, mainly in Nizi (24), Rwampara (14), Bania (10), Nia-Nia (8), Bambu (4), Fataki (4), Logo (2), Mangala (2) Mongbwalu (2), Lita (2) and Komanda (1), 45 deaths among which, 73,3% community.

o Nord-Kivu: 18 new confirmed cases were reported (Katwa 9, Butembo 4, Musienene 4, and 1 Beni) as well as 14 deaths, of which 6 community and 8 in the CTE (Ebola treatment centre).
The provincial cumulative total reaches 275 confirmed cases and 172 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 62,5%.

o Haut-Uélé: 6 new confirmed cases and 3 deaths of which 66,7% community were reported.
The provincial cumulative total rises to 27 confirmed cases and 15 deaths, representing a case fatality rate of 55,6 %.

o Sud-Kivu and Tshopo: No new confirmed case nor death was reported.
The cumulative totals remain at 5 cases, 4 deaths and 1 recovered in Tshopo and 3 cases of which 1 death in Sud-Kivu, where the Miti-Murhesa health zone totals 55 days without a new confirmed case.

• Analysis: Ituri remains the epicentre of the outbreak, concentrating 89,3 % of cumulative cases and 75,3 % of new confirmations of the day.
Contact tracing performance remains insufficient and requires a strengthening of surveillance activities.

EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Declared on 15 May 2026, the 17th outbreak of Ebola virus disease (MVE) due to Bundibugyo ebolavirus continues its course in a complex humanitarian and security context.
Initially confined to the health zone of Mongbwalu (Ituri), it spread to five provinces (Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo), now affecting 47 health zones.
Population movements, insecurity, artisanal mining activities and cross-border trade with Uganda and South Sudan continue to favour transmission.
Multisectoral coordination remains mobilised in order to strengthen surveillance, intensify response interventions and limit the spread of the outbreak.

[FIGURE: Figure 1 — Chronology of events of the Bundibugyo Ebola virus disease outbreak]

## 2.3 Mapping of confirmed cases

The spatial distribution confirms transmission mainly concentrated in Ituri, particularly in the health zones of Bunia, Rwampara, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Nyankunde and Lita, with continued transmission in the already affected zones of Haut-Uélé.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 2 — HEALTH ZONES THAT REPORTED CONFIRMED CASES (AS OF 22/07/2026)]

The recent appearance of new foci in Haut-Uélé confirms a progressive extension of the affected zones, highlighting the need to maintain simultaneously intensive interventions at the level of the epicentre and preparedness activities in neighbouring provinces.

## 2.4 Temporal analysis — epidemic curves

The epidemic curve shows sustained transmission during weeks W25 to W30, with fluctuations linked to reporting delays and the progressive consolidation of data.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 3 — EPIDEMIC CURVE BY WEEK OF NOTIFICATION]

[FIGURE: FIGURE 4 EPIDEMIC CURVE BY DATE OF ONSET OF SYMPTOMS (DHIS2 LINE LIST)]

The outbreak remains in a phase of sustained transmission, with a high level of virus circulation.
Recent fluctuations must be interpreted with caution due to reporting delays and the progressive consolidation of data.

## 2.5 Demographic characteristics

The age pyramid shows a predominance of working-age adults (18–50 years).
Minors under 18 years and people aged over 50 years are proportionally less affected.

[FIGURE: FIGURE 5 — CONFIRMED CASES BY SEX AND AGE GROUP]

[FIGURE: FIGURE 6 — DEATHS BY SEX AND AGE GROUP (AMONG CONFIRMED CASES)]

The distribution of cases by sex remains balanced.
The predominance of cases among working-age adults reflects more frequent community and occupational exposures, whilst the proportion of paediatric cases testifies to the persistence of intrafamilial transmission.

→ Haut-Uele: 12 samples received and analysed, among which 6 positive (4 live and 2 deaths), representing a positivity of 50,0 %.

→ Tshopo: 3 samples received and analysed, among which 1 from the province of Tshuapa.

# 7 Response activities by pillar

COORDINATION

→ Ituri: Arrival of the new National Incident Manager (IM) in Bunia, Professor Steve Ahuka; The Minister of Public Health, Hygiene and Social Welfare as well as Professor Pierre Akilimali (IM) were received in audience by the President of Uganda on 22 July 2026 to review the situation of the Bundibugyo Ebola Virus Disease (MVE-B 17); Harmonisation of epidemiological data between the provinces of Ituri and Nord-Kivu and the national level.

PCI (infection prevention and control) / WASH

→ Ituri: provision of 10 DLM at the Dele/Kinama market; start of training of 27 PPL in Drodro; 25 rings opened, 29 ESS followed up/supported, 8 assessments, 4 ESS and 6 means of transport decontaminated, 117 PPL trained and 25/159 households decontaminated within 48h.

→ Nord-Kivu: Start of the first training cohort of 32 PCI supervisors and focal points from the health zones of Beni and the second cohort of 80 for the ZS (health zone) Katwa, Butembo and Musienene with WHO support.

→ Tshopo: meeting of the PCI pillar; provision of supplies to 3 ESS; assessments of CS Boyoma (16 %), CSR Rvd Mokili (43 %) and CTE HCKis (82 %); 2 ESS decontaminated and 5 triage units functional out of 79.

SAFE AND DIGNIFIED BURIALS (EDS)

→ Ituri: 75 death alerts received, 68 EDS conducted, 43 swabs and 91 % of EDS conducted; community resistance in Bambu and Rwampara; continuation of construction work on the decontamination base; start of training of two EDS teams in the ZS of Tchomia.

→ Nord-Kivu: 39 Swabs performed out of 40 death alerts escalated 1 failed swab in Butembo,

→ Tshopo: continuation of required Coordination for the management of community deaths and the safe transport of bodies.

CONTINUITY OF ESSENTIAL HEALTH SERVICES (CSSE)

→ Ituri: continuation of supervision of Health Zone.

COMMUNICATION (RCCE / CREC)

→ Ituri: Briefing of 30 FARDC in Nizi; 675 people reached through VAD, 917 in educational talks, 1 765 through mass awareness-raising, 166 community alerts escalated and 3 feedbacks clarified; briefing of 50 chiefs in Mambasa and 90 RECO (community health worker) in Adja.

→ Nord-Kivu: Educational talk with members of ATAMOV on the risks faced by motorcycle taxi drivers when transporting on motorbikes patients with MVE and the bodies of persons who died from the same disease; Community dialogue with women in the village of Elungu, in the AS (health area) Aloya on prevention measures against MVE and reporting alerts for any patient presenting signs of MVE.

HOLISTIC CARE (PECH)

→ Ituri: 12 newly recovered, 551 patients in isolation, 24 deaths among discharges; 1022 hot meals were served to patients including 128 to suspected cases, 156 to Confirmed cases, 691 to PPL and 47 to companions.

→ Nord-Kivu: 36 admissions, 50 discharges, 168 hospitalised patients, including 17 confirmed and 151 suspected; continued monitoring of case management in CTE/CT.

→ Tshopo: 12 hot meals were served to patients including 6 to suspected cases and 6 to confirmed cases.

→ Tshopo: 324 people were reached during door-to-door awareness-raising in the météo and sotraco blocks in the city of Kisangani; 15.868 people were reached during mass awareness-raising held during Sunday Health worship celebrations.
(ZS Mangobo, Kabondo, Tshopo, Lubunga and Makioso Kisangani)

RESEARCH, INNOVATION & VACCINATION

→ Ituri: Studies on community reluctance and perceptions: Results dissemination process (WHO and UNICEF support);
Anthropological study on the BDVD index case: near completion (WHO support);
Partner Clinical Trials (Vaccine): In progress;
EBO-PEP Clinical Trials: In progress (ALIMA support)

LOGISTICS

→ Ituri: Ensure mobility of the different pillars.

→ Nord-Kivu: Receipt of nutritional care supplies consisting of Plumpy Nut from Bunia supported by UG-PDSS

→ Tshopo: 4 vehicles and 1 Ambulance were made available to the different pillars to ensure case transfer and mobility of pillars in the field.

PREVENTION OF SEXUAL EXPLOITATION AND ABUSE (PSEA / PRSEAH)

→ Ituri: Awareness-raising at the Bembey site on PSEA.
In total, 135 people were reached including 63 Women, 16 girls, 38 men and 18 boys; Awareness-raising in the CNCA health area, health zone of Bunia for pregnant women on the prevention of SEA, mechanisms as well as the referral pathway.
In total, 26 participants including 24 girls (PWD: 1) and 2 boys; Training of 27 hygiene workers including 15 men and 12 women of the Rwampara CTE on general aspects of PSEA, complaint management mechanisms and confidentiality the training concluded with the signing of the code of conduct; Training of Red Cross volunteers in Bunia on the data collection tool for SEA/SH Risk analysis for the ZS of Rwampara.

# 8 Main challenges, impacts and required actions


| N° | Challenges | Impact | Required actions |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance towards post-mortem sampling (EDS/swabs), community resistance and insecurity targeting EDS teams (attack at Muchanga bridge, paralysis of activities in Nyankunde) | Delay in confirmation, underestimation of cases, disruption of key activities | Intensify RCCE, involve religious and community leaders, secure teams, increase the number of EDS teams |
| 2 | Non-payment of providers (strike in the ZS of Bunia and Rwampara; resumption announced following the intervention of the military governor of Ituri) | Interruption of response activities, including safe and dignified burials | Regularise payment of providers; secure dedicated funding |
| 3 | Insufficient CTE/CT capacity: occupancy of 119,1 % in Nord-Kivu (bed capacity: 141) and 77,7 % in Ituri (551 patients for 709 beds); | Admission delays, increased risk of nosocomial transmission | Accelerate construction and expansion of CTEs, deploy temporary structures, systematically report bed capacity |
| 4 | Contact tracing performance low in Ituri 73,3 % ; Nord-Kivu 77,7% | Uninterrupted transmission chains | Train, deploy and motivate community health workers (RECO); strengthened supervision; investigate the decline observed in Ituri |
| 5 | Shortage of ambulances and prepositioning at PoCs | Delays in transfer and isolation | Preposition ambulances (including at PoE/PoC), deploy CTs by ZS |
| 6 | Insufficient supply of essential generic drugs (MEG) and medical supplies | Weakening of overall care | Advocacy and urgent supply of essential medicines |
| 7 | Shortage of IPC supplies (PPE, chlorine) and limited functional triage units (175/1 170, or 15 %) | High risk of nosocomial infections (121 PPL cases including 36 deaths) | Urgent supply, strengthening IPC training |
| 8 | Geographical extension (Haut-Uélé, Tshopo) and high mobility | Risk of urban, river and cross-border spread | Activate the 23 priority PoE/PoC in Haut-Uélé; strengthen cross-border coordination |
| 9 | Installation of local laboratories (Butembo, Mambasa and Logo) | Long confirmation times, undetected transmission | Accelerate the deployment of decentralised diagnostic capacities |
| 10 | Insufficient financial resources | Limitation of pillar implementation | Urgent resource mobilisation, advocacy with partners |
| 11 | Insecurity and limited access (CODECO, ADF) | Restriction of operations | Strengthening security coordination and humanitarian access |
| 12 | Continuity of essential health services (CEHS) compromised | Increase in indirect mortality (non-Ebola) | Effective implementation of free healthcare, strengthening CEHS |
